newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia taskforce urges less bureaucracy.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia taskforce urges less bureaucracy.

text.p: An Australian government taskforce on Friday urged sweeping cuts to government paperwork for small business and the costs of complying with bureaucratic regulations.

The taskforce, set up by the government after its March election win, made 62 recommendations, including simplified government forms, exempting meals from fringe benefits tax, standardised state and national requirements in some areas and reviews of various government regulations to reduce paperwork for business.
"The small business community is frustrated and overwhelmed by the complexity and cost of dealing with government regulation and paperwork," the taskforce said in a statement.
It found complying with government regulations and paperwork cost small business an average A$7,000 a year, including A$3,000 paid for external advice.
Small Business Minister Geoff Prosser said in a statement he would consider the recommendations and take a submission to cabinet early next year.
